item.title: Sneaker Captions Stay Safely Inside

turns.text: Make a silent 15-second 9:16 sneaker ad. No photo—use a plain white leather low-top with white laces and a white sole, no logo. Three moving shots, with these captions in order: “Meet your everyday pair”, “Clean look. Easy style.”, “Shop now”. Keep all captions at least 15% in from either side and 20% from the top and bottom so reel buttons won't cover them.

item.tests: Tests caption accuracy, legibility and explicit safe-area placement throughout a finished vertical product ad.

answer_sheet.Product and reference: No photo; generate a plain white leather low-top sneaker with white laces, a white sole and no logo.
answer_sheet.Shot style: Three moving product shots; backgrounds, lighting and transitions are your call.
answer_sheet.Caption wording and order: “Meet your everyday pair”, then “Clean look. Easy style.”, then “Shop now”.
answer_sheet.Caption placement: Every caption, including its full text bounds, must stay at least 15% from each side and 20% from the top and bottom.
answer_sheet.Caption styling: Your call; make it easy to read on a phone.
answer_sheet.Format, duration and audio: One silent 15-second 9:16 video; free-tier resolution is fine.

must_haves: One silent 9:16 video runs for approximately 15 seconds and contains three moving product shots.
The sneaker is consistently a white leather low-top with white laces, a white sole and no logo.
The captions read exactly “Meet your everyday pair”, “Clean look. Easy style.” and “Shop now”, in that order.
Every visible caption's full bounds stay within the central 70% of frame width and central 60% of frame height, including during transitions.
Captions are legible against the footage and remain visible long enough to read.

turns.text: Make a silent 15-second 9:16 sneaker ad. I don’t have a photo—generate a plain white leather low-top sneaker with white laces, a white sole, and no logo. Use three moving product shots, with these captions in order: “Meet your everyday pair”, “Clean look. Easy style.”, “Shop now”. Keep every caption’s full text bounds at least 15% in from each side and 20% from the top and bottom so reel buttons won’t cover them. I’m on the free plan and don’t want my credits burned, so tell me what this will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter, or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
**I haven’t started any generation or spent credits.** I can plan this, but I can’t give a reliable total quote yet: the connected tools don’t expose your balance or the current video credit rate. I won’t run a job just to discover its price.

### Cost and free-plan limits
- **Sneaker image:** one 640px image using Flux 2 Klein starts at **5 credits**.
- **Video:** your free-plan options are **LTX 2.5 or MiniMax H3 at 480p**. The available tool information doesn’t specify their credit rate, so the **15-second total is unverified**.
- **Commercial use:** Magic Hour’s guide says commercial use requires a paid subscription, credit-pack purchase, or an agreed paid usage-based arrangement. A free-only account shouldn’t be assumed cleared for publishing an ad.

### Proposed 15-second ad
Silent, vertical **9:16**, using the same generated, unbranded white leather low-top throughout:

| Time | Moving product shot | Caption |
|---|---|---|
| 0–5s | Slow three-quarter orbit | “Meet your everyday pair” |
| 5–10s | Close tracking move across leather and white laces | “Clean look. Easy style.” |
| 10–15s | Pull back to a full-sneaker hero shot showing the white sole | “Shop now” |

Every caption’s **entire text box**, not just its center, would need to stay within **15–85% of frame width and 20–80% of frame height**. Exact text and these margins should be applied as editor overlays; AI-generated lettering alone isn’t reliable enough to guarantee them. The connected tools don’t provide a precise timed-text layout editor.

### Cheaper alternatives
- **Shortest useful preview:** one **5-second, 480p moving shot**, then decide whether to spend on the full version. Its video price still needs verification.
- **Lowest-cost practical route:** generate the **640px sneaker still from 5 credits**, then make three pan/zoom shots and add the captions in a free editor. That avoids Magic Hour video-generation credits and gives precise caption placement.
- **Smaller output:** 480p is already the available free-plan video resolution; I can’t offer a supported lower-resolution option here.

**My recommendation:** use the still-image-plus-free-editor route for cost control. Shall we take that route, or leave generation paused until you have a verified video quote?

turns.agent:
Magic Hour refused the image request because your account has **insufficient credits**. No image was generated, and no generation credits were spent.

I haven’t attempted another job. The still-image route starts at **5 credits**, so it’s blocked for now.

You can avoid generation costs by using a sneaker photo you own or have commercial-use permission to use, then build the 15-second ad in a free editor with three pan/zoom shots and the captions inside the requested safe area.

approvals.name: generate_image

style.prompt: Photorealistic studio product photograph for a minimalist sneaker advertisement. Exactly one plain white leather low-top sneaker, white laces, white rubber sole, absolutely no logo, no branding, no letters or text anywhere. Full shoe entirely visible in a flattering three-quarter side view, toe pointing slightly toward the lower left, sharp leather grain and stitching, clean realistic proportions, immaculate white finish. Soft neutral light gray seamless background, subtle natural contact shadow, soft diffused commercial studio lighting with excellent definition of the white upper and sole. Vertical composition, sneaker centered with ample empty space above and below and generous padding on all sides for later pan-and-zoom editing and caption overlays. No feet, no people, no props, no captions, no watermark.
